originalTitle: Edelweiss Alternatives raises over Rs 1,200 crore for second Discovery fund; backs Arboreal Bio
simplifiedContent: Edelweiss Alternatives, a company that helps manage investments, has collected over Rs 1,200 crore for its second Discovery Fund. This fund is used to invest in other companies. The company has already used some of this money to invest Rs 230 crore in a company called Arboreal Bio Innovations. This investment will help Arboreal Bio expand its manufacturing and develop new products. This matter because it shows that Edelweiss Alternatives is actively investing the money it has collected, which could potentially lead to growth and returns for its investors.

originalTitle: SBI raises Rs 4,691 crore via Tier 1 bonds at 7.75% coupon
simplifiedContent: The State Bank of India (SBI) has raised a large amount of money, Rs 4,691 crore, by selling special bonds called Tier 1 bonds. These bonds will pay investors an annual interest rate of 7.75%. Many institutional investors, such as banks and investment companies, were very interested in buying these bonds, with the demand being more than twice the amount available. This shows that investors have a lot of confidence in SBI and are willing to lend them money. The successful sale of these bonds is a positive sign for SBI and its ability to raise funds.

originalTitle: Rupee firms, volatility expectations tick up heading into Fed decision
simplifiedContent: The Indian rupee recently reached its highest value in three weeks, which is good news for India's economy. This happened because Indian stocks did well, and some banks sold US dollars, which helped reduce demand for dollars. At the same time, oil prices increased due to tensions in the Middle East, but India's main stock index still managed to rise because other global markets were not doing as well. The increase in the rupee's value and the rise in India's stock index may be partly due to investors preparing for an upcoming decision by the US Federal Reserve. This decision is making investors a bit uncertain, which is why they are adjusting their investments.

originalTitle: SBI raises  ₹4,691 crore through the issuance of tier-1 bonds. Details here
simplifiedContent: The State Bank of India (SBI) has raised a large amount of money, ₹4,691 crore, by selling special bonds called AT1 bonds. These bonds pay an interest rate of 7.75% and will be paid forever, unless SBI decides to stop paying. Many big investors were interested in buying these bonds, which helped SBI raise the money. The bonds have a high rating of AA+ from two reputable rating agencies, CRISIL and CARE Ratings, which means they are considered to be a relatively safe investment. This fundraising is important for SBI as it helps the bank to strengthen its financial position.

originalTitle: Nifty seen breaking the 24,000 expiry jinx
simplifiedContent: The Nifty is a measure of how well the Indian stock market is doing, and it has been having trouble getting past a certain point, 24,000, for the past five months. This has been happening since the war in West Asia started. Some people who follow the market think that things might be different this month, though. They hope that the Nifty will be able to get above 24,000 by the end of August. This matters because it could be a good sign for the overall health of the stock market if the Nifty can break through this barrier.

originalTitle: Bajaj Housing Finance Q1 results: Profit jumps 23% YoY to  ₹715 crore
simplifiedContent: Bajaj Housing Finance, a company that provides home loans, has released its financial results for the first quarter of the financial year. The company's profit increased by 23% compared to the same period last year, reaching ₹715 crore. This means the company made more money than it did a year ago. The company's net interest income, which is the difference between the interest it earns and the interest it pays, also increased by 9% to ₹968 crore. This is important because it shows that the company is performing well and making more money, which could be good news for investors who own shares in the company.
